section: U.S. law: AVAs and the TTB label
title: TTB Boot Camp for Wineries: Beyond the Basics-American Viticultural Areas (AVAs)
why: The federal agency that writes the rules walks through appellations of origin, AVAs and how an AVA petition is filed and approved.

title: The Wines of Washington
why: GuildSomm's guide to Washington: the rain shadow, irrigation, the Missoula Flood soils and the main AVAs and grapes.

section: New York, other states, Canada and Mexico
title: New York Wines: Finger Lakes AVA
why: The New York Wine & Grape Foundation tours the Finger Lakes AVA, home of the nested Cayuga Lake and Seneca Lake AVAs.

title: The Wines of Chile
why: GuildSomm maps Chile's regions and valleys from north to south, the backbone of the Decree 464 map in this section.

title: Central Otago Wine Region
why: New Zealand Winegrowers shows Central Otago and its subregions, each with its own climate, aspect and altitude.

title: Understanding South Africa Part 1 for WSET L3 - Intro to South Africa With Working Written Question
why: A wine educator's overview of South Africa's regions and climate, with a map, as groundwork for the Wine of Origin ladder.

title: Harvest and Pressing in Champagne
why: The Comité Champagne shows hand harvest and the regulated pressing, where the cuvée and the taille are kept apart.

title: The Wines of Sherry
why: GuildSomm covers the Sherry triangle, flor and oxidative aging, the solera and the special categories.

title: MADEIRA WINE EXPLAINED - what it is, what it tastes like and how to drink it!
why: Explains how Madeira is made and aged, then tastes through several of its styles.

title: Introduction to Aromatized Wines
why: Uses the WSET framework to explain what an aromatized wine is and how vermouth, quinquina and americano differ.

title: Making Japanese Sake
why: The Japan Sake and Shochu Makers Association follows sake brewing day by day, from rice polishing to the yeast starter, the mash and pressing.

section: Spirits: distillation, aging laws, aperitifs and digestifs
title: Pot Still vs Column Still: What's The Difference???
why: Compares pot and column stills and shows how the still choice changes the flavor of the spirit.

title: The Wines of Champagne
why: GuildSomm explains Champagne's cold climate, chalk subsoil, villages and how the wine is made and labeled.

title: BURGUNDY'S COTE D'OR - WINE IN 10
why: A Master of Wine walks the Côte d'Or from Dijon to Santenay, including the Côte de Nuits villages and their Grands Crus.

title: The Wines of Bordeaux's Right Bank
why: GuildSomm covers Saint-Émilion and Pomerol: their soils, Merlot and the Saint-Émilion classification.

title: The Wines of Alsace
why: GuildSomm explains Alsace's patchwork of soils, its Grand Cru appellation and the Vendanges Tardives and SGN labels.

title: The Wines of Northern Rhône
why: GuildSomm goes cru by cru through the northern Rhône: Côte-Rôtie, Condrieu, Château-Grillet, Hermitage, Cornas and Saint-Péray.

title: Jura Wine Explained: Vin Jaune, Savagnin & the Region’s Icons
why: A Master of Wine visits Jura's vineyards and makers and explains Vin Jaune, its long aging under a veil of yeast, and Savagnin.
